company_name: Booster Private Land and Property Fund
units: NZD per unit unless stated; net assets in millions
method: NAV-per-unit compounding with quarterly distribution stream and exit price-to-NAV multiple, discounted at cost of equity. NOT an FCF DCF.
valuation_philosophy: The Private Land and Property Fund (PLP) is an NZX-listed managed investment scheme (unit trust) whose sole asset is 100% of the units in the unlisted Private Land and Property Portfolio (PLPP), a wholesale fund holding NZ agricultural, horticultural and industrial property (viticulture, kiwifruit, avocado, dairy farmland, hops, and one large Rolleston logistics warehouse at 32.49% of net assets). It is a NAV vehicle, not an operating company. Its reported 'revenue' is distribution pass-through from PLPP plus a management-fee rebate, and its net income is dominated by fair-value (FVTPL) swings on the PLPP holding -- a $2.23m fair-value LOSS in FY2026 and $3.90m loss in FY2025. FY2025's operating cash flow of -$90.5m is capital deployment (a ~$98.6m asset purchase funded by a $103.9m unit issue), not an operating loss; annualising or extrapolating it would be meaningless. An owner-FCF DCF was therefore rejected and the fund is routed to the NAV/NTA + exit-discount model, the same family this repo uses for BIF.NZ, MLN.NZ and AFI.NZ -- with one difference from BIF.NZ: PLP pays real quarterly cash distributions (~2.5% of NAV, funded by rents and crop proceeds), so the model discounts an interim distribution stream plus a year-5 exit at a scenario price-to-NAV multiple, at a cost of equity built up for NZ unlisted rural property (14.0%, see wacc_rationale). The central fact of this valuation is that the units trade at a slight PREMIUM (~0.2-1.4%) to NAV, when listed vehicles holding unlisted assets almost always trade at a discount. That premium is almost certainly a free-float artefact: ~95.5% of units sit in four related Booster vehicles (Booster KiwiSaver 56.33%, Asset Custodian Nominees 21.67%, Booster SuperScheme 11.18%, Booster Investment Scheme 6.32%), so the on-market price is set by a sliver of thin trading and is not doing real price discovery. The usual listed-fund value thesis -- buy at a discount to NAV and capture the convergence -- is simply unavailable here: there is no discount to close. What remains is the asset-level return stream itself, and that stream has been poor: NAV per unit has fallen for three consecutive fiscal years (FY2023 peak $1.4002 to FY2026 $1.2859), the trailing 5-year return after tax is 4.93% (5.41% before tax) against a 6.50% p.a. target, and the trailing 3-year return averages roughly -0.7% p.a. Discounting a realistic recovery of that stream at a rate that prices the illiquidity, the manager-quoted Level 2 marks, the Rolleston concentration and the agricultural cyclicality produces a base-case intrinsic value of roughly $0.84 (-36%) and a probability-weighted value of roughly $0.80 (-38%). This is not a reverse-engineered bearish output: even at a bare 9% cost of equity with every risk premium stripped out, the base-case stream is worth only ~$1.04, still ~20% below the $1.304 price (see required_return_table). The honest conclusion is that at ~parity to a NAV that has declined three years running, yielding 2.5%, with a below-target record, rising look-through gearing, live FMA litigation against the manager, and no discount to capture, the current price offers limited-to-negative expected return at any defensible discount rate.

inputs.nav_current_basis_source: Manager's unit price effective 18 June 2026, after the June-2026 independent revaluation of the Rolleston (Iport Drive) industrial warehouse (+$2.35m, +1.15% of NAV) lifted the unit price from $1.2862 to $1.3010. Used in preference to the 31-Mar-2026 unit price of $1.2859 because it is the most current observable NAV and embeds a post-balance-date mark the annual accounts do not reflect.
inputs.nav_vs_nta_note: The audited IFRS NTA ($1.29) and the manager's unit price ($1.2859 at 31-Mar, $1.3010 from 18-Jun) differ slightly because for unit-pricing purposes some assets are held at fair value while IFRS classifies them as PP&E at cost (FS note 6). The gap is small (<1%) but means the traded NAV is a manager's pricing construct, not the audited balance sheet number.
inputs.net_debt_treatment_note: Net debt is set to zero for valuation purposes: this is a per-unit NAV model and both the Fund-level cash ($1.022m) and the PLPP look-through borrowings are already embedded in NAV per unit. Deducting debt or adding cash on top of a NAV-based value would double-count. NOTE ON BASES: the CSV's TotalDebt (13.75) is deliberately the LOOK-THROUGH PLPP-level borrowing figure while TotalLiabilities (0.200) is Fund-level -- they are on different bases by design and must not be netted against each other or read as an inconsistency.
inputs.look_through_gearing_note: PLPP-level borrowings rose from $3.75m to $13.75m during FY2026 -- nearly 4x in one year -- on look-through total assets of ~$214.5m, i.e. ~6.4% gearing. Still modest in absolute terms, but the trajectory matters and the Fund-level balance sheet (total liabilities $0.2m) completely hides it. The BNZ facility can extend to 50% of secured property value, so capacity for further gearing is large.
inputs.distribution_note: FY2026 distributions of $5.294m (~3.25 cents/unit, ~2.5% of NAV, paid quarterly) are funded by rental income and crop proceeds passed up from PLPP. They exceeded profit after tax ($1.314m) -- i.e. they are substantially an income pass-through / return of capital rather than covered by accounting earnings, because accounting profit is depressed by fair-value losses. Modelled as a 2.5% yield on projected NAV in the base case (2.75% bull, 2.25% bear).
inputs.fees_note: Total fund charges are 1.25% of NAV p.a. (manager's basic fee 1.02%; PDS Feb-2026 estimates ~1.22% forward), no performance fee. This is a permanent drag between gross asset returns and unitholder returns and is embedded in the NAV growth assumptions below (all growth paths are net-of-fee), not ignored.
inputs.ownership_structure: ~95.5% of units held by four related Booster vehicles: Booster KiwiSaver Scheme 56.33%, Asset Custodian Nominees 21.67%, Booster SuperScheme 11.18%, Booster Investment Scheme 6.32%. Genuine independent free float ~4.5%.
inputs.sbc: not applicable -- unit trust with no employees or equity compensation; the manager (BIML) is paid via management fees
inputs.interest_income: not applicable -- Fund-level cash is $1.0m (~0.5% of net assets); interest revenue is immaterial and inside NAV
inputs.fcf_dcf_note: Not applicable. No EBITDA, capex, working capital or owner-FCF concept exists for this vehicle. FY2025 OCF of -$90.505m is deployment of a $103.9m unit subscription into a ~$98.6m asset purchase, NOT an operating loss -- it must never be trended, annualised or used as an FCF base.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-08-26T01:31:11Z (Yahoo regularMarketPrice, regular NZX session, fresh regularMarketTime; occasional null daily bars reflect thin free-float trading, not a frozen quote)
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2026-03-31 (FY2026 audited); NAV base updated to 18-Jun-2026 manager pricing
inputs.units: millions (NZD) for fund-level aggregates; NZD per unit for per-unit figures
inputs.notes: Model: NAV/NTA + exit discount (nav_compounding_with_distributions), routed per .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md row 'LIC, investment trust, closed-end fund, VC unit trust'. Chosen because PLP is a pass-through unit trust over unlisted property whose income statement is dominated by FVTPL revaluation noise and whose cash flow statement mixes capital deployment with operations -- the same reasoning as BIF.NZ, MLN.NZ and AFI.NZ in this repo. Quote currency and financials are both NZD; no currency layer.

historical_growth.target_return_note: Stated target is 6.50% p.a. after fees, before tax, over rolling 7-year periods. The fund is running materially below target: 5-year average 5.41% before tax, 3-year annualised ~2.1% before tax (Dec-2025 client update). NAV per unit peaked at $1.4002 (FY2023) and has declined three consecutive years since.
historical_growth.eps_note: Revenue/EPS CAGRs are not meaningful -- reported revenue and net income are dominated by FVTPL revaluation swings on the PLPP holding (FY2025 NI -$1.688m, FY2026 +$1.314m, both driven by fair-value marks). A NI-based CAGR would be Level-2-marking noise, not signal.
historical_growth.equity_cagr_note: Total net assets grew mainly through unit issuance (units on issue grew from 35.7m FY2019 to 163.1m FY2026), so total-equity CAGR measures capital raising, not investment performance. NAV PER UNIT is the only per-unitholder-relevant growth measure.
historical_growth.fcf_note: Not applicable -- no FCF concept exists for this vehicle (see inputs.fcf_dcf_note).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: nav_per_unit_cagr_7yr_fy19_fy26 (capital-only NAV growth, excludes the ~2.5% distribution yield; the total-return analogue is the 6.14% since-inception average return). Used as the screener's forward-growth proxy with the caveat that the last three years averaged -2.8% p.a.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: The 7-year NAV/unit CAGR (+3.81%) and the 3-year CAGR (-2.80%) point in opposite directions -- the fund's entire positive record was built in FY2020-FY2023 and has been eroding since. Scenario growth paths are anchored between these two realities rather than on either alone, and NOT on the 6.5% target, which has not been achieved over any recent trailing window.

wacc_rationale.methodology: Cost of equity built up from a NZ risk-free rate and an equity risk premium appropriate to income-producing property (sub-market beta), plus four additive premiums specific to PLP's structure. All flows are NZD and the discount rate is built from NZD anchors -- no currency mismatch.

component_rationale.nz_property_equity_risk_premium: 5.0% rather than a full ~6% equity ERP: the underlying assets are income-producing property with contracted rents and crop proceeds, a lower-beta claim than general equities; the asset-specific risks are then priced explicitly as separate premiums rather than smuggled into the ERP.
component_rationale.illiquidity_near_absent_free_float_premi: ~4.5% genuine free float once the four related Booster holders (95.5%) are excluded; the NZX order book prints null bars on some days, direct withdrawals over $50k/yr carry 1-5% exit fees, and full realisation of PLPP assets could take >6 months by the manager's own disclosure. A holder needing size liquidity has no reliable exit at NAV (+1.5-2.5% range used at 2.0%).
component_rationale.valuation_opacity_level2_manager_marks_p: NAV is a Level 2 fair value set at the manager's own quoted PLPP redemption price -- informed by external property valuations the manager selects, but assessed and adopted by the manager itself, flagged as a key audit matter every year. There is no market clearing price behind the number, though the external-valuation input and real rental cash flows make this less severe than BIF.NZ's pure Level 3 marks (+1.0-1.5% range used at 1.0%).
component_rationale.asset_concentration_rolleston_premium: The Iport Drive Rolleston warehouse alone is 32.49% of net assets -- a single tenant/asset event (vacancy, adverse rent review, cap-rate move) moves the whole fund's NAV materially. The June-2026 +$2.35m uplift that forms part of the current NAV base is itself a mark on this one asset (+0.5-1.5% range used at 1.0%).
component_rationale.agricultural_climate_commodity_premium: Marlborough viticulture is oversupplied with US tariffs at 15% on NZ wine; avocado markets are weak by the manager's own description; dairy income depends on the Fonterra payout; climate/biosecurity risk is inherent to orchards and vineyards. Used at the bottom of the +0.5-1.5% range because the portfolio is diversified across five crop/asset categories and the largest asset (Rolleston) is industrial, already premia-ed separately (+0.5%).

wacc_rationale.robustness_note: The conclusion does not depend on the premiums: at a bare 9.5% (risk-free + property ERP, zero structural premiums) the base-case stream is worth ~$1.01-$1.04 versus the $1.304 price. See required_return_table.

base.nav_growth_rationale: Capital-only NAV growth (net of the ~1.25% fee drag and after paying out the ~2.5% distribution), sitting between the depressed 3-year experience (-2.8% p.a.) and the 7-year average (+3.8% p.a.). Implied TOTAL return (growth + 2.5% distribution) ramps from ~3.0% to ~4.5% -- a recovery toward, but never reaching, the 6.5% target the fund has missed for five years. Supports: maturing kiwifruit/hop plantings, Rolleston industrial rent-growth tailwind, NZ-India FTA. Restrains: Marlborough wine oversupply, weak avocados, dairy payout cuts, rising PLPP interest costs.
base.exit_rationale: The units have traded at ~parity to NAV throughout their (short) listed price history, sustained by the captive 95.5% related-party register. Base case honestly assumes that persists.

bull.nav_growth_rationale: The manager's thesis works: plantings reach full productive capacity, kiwifruit strength (record Zespri forecasts) and industrial revaluations continue, wine/avocado cycles turn. Implied total return of ~5.75-7.25% p.a. approaches and modestly exceeds the 6.5% target -- i.e. the bull case is 'the fund finally does what it says on the tin', not a heroic re-rating.
bull.exit_rationale: Capped near parity as instructed: even in a good outcome, a listed wrapper over unlisted rural land with a 4.5% free float does not command a durable premium. 1.03x reflects at most the thin-float premium already observed today.

bear.nav_growth_rationale: The FY2024-FY2026 pattern extends: further downward revaluations in wine (oversupply + 15% US tariffs), avocados and Kerikeri kiwifruit (already cut $1.4m in 2025), dairy payout softness, and rising interest costs on the quadrupled PLPP borrowings eating distributable income. Front-loaded (-4% Y1) because the vulnerable marks are current; implied total return ~-1.75% to +1.25% p.a., consistent with the realised 3-year average of -0.7%.
bear.exit_rationale: A discount opens for the first time: if any of the four related Booster holders became a seller (e.g. KiwiSaver liquidity needs, or fallout from the Feb-2027 FMA trial forcing restructuring at BIML), the 4.5% free float could not absorb the stock and the price would have to find genuine clearing demand -- which for an illiquid, manager-marked rural vehicle is plausibly 0.85-0.92x NAV. Used 0.88x.

projections.distributions_note: Distributions are modelled as a yield on each year's closing NAV, paid at year end -- an approximation of the actual quarterly cadence that slightly understates PV. They are real, established cash returns (quarterly since listing, $5.294m in FY2026), which is why -- unlike BIF.NZ -- this model has an interim cash flow component and terminal value is ~85-86% of value rather than 100%.
projections.unit_count_note: Per-unit basis throughout. Unit issuance/redemption at manager-struck NAV is value-neutral per unit and is not modelled as dilution or accretion.

valuation.formula: IV = SUM_t[ dist_t / (1+CoE)^t ] + NAV_year5 x exit_P/NAV / (1+CoE)^5, CoE = 14.0%

base.implied_exit_multiple: 1.00x P/NAV -- a NAV valuation, not an earnings or FCF multiple

valuation.street_basis_note: No house/street SBC split exists for a unit trust (no SBC). street_intrinsic_value equals intrinsic_value in every scenario and band_position is null -- the band collapses by construction, as for other SBC-zero tickers in this repo.

entry_price.methodology: Entry price = PV at 15% of the base-case distribution stream + PV at 15% of the base-case year-5 exit value. No net-debt adjustment (net debt is inside NAV). Because the model's own CoE (14%) is close to the hurdle, the entry price sits only slightly below intrinsic value.

required_return_table.description: Base-case IV (distribution stream + 1.00x NAV exit on the base growth path) at alternative required returns. Even at 9% -- risk-free plus a bare property ERP with NO illiquidity, opacity, concentration or agricultural premium -- the stream is worth ~$1.04, still ~20% below the $1.304 price. The negative verdict is driven by the gap between the fund's delivered returns and any defensible required return, not by the premium build-up.

sensitivity.methodology: IV = PV(2.5%-of-NAV distributions) + PV(year-5 NAV x exit P/NAV), NAV compounding at a flat rate g from the $1.3010 base, discounted at the 14% CoE. The two dominant levers: realised NAV growth and the exit multiple.
sensitivity.matrix_note: Even the most generous cell shown -- 4.5% p.a. NAV growth (near the pre-decline era) with a 1.05x exit premium -- yields $1.01, below the current $1.304 price. Reaching the current price at a 14% CoE requires assumptions outside any realised experience of this fund.

cost_of_equity_sensitivity.description: Base-case IV as the cost of equity varies +/-3pp around the 14% central estimate.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear is lifted above the house default 15% to 30% because the adverse evidence is already realised, not hypothetical: three consecutive annual NAV declines, a 3-year return averaging -0.7% p.a. versus a 6.5% target, PLPP borrowings up ~4x in one year, two crop categories (wine, avocado) in manager-acknowledged oversupply, and FMA civil proceedings (75 causes of action) against the manager going to trial February 2027 while PLPP keeps transacting with the same related-party network. Bull is cut to 20% because it requires the fund to achieve a target it has missed over every recent trailing window. Weights sum to 1.0 and weighted_iv recomputes exactly from the scenario IVs: 0.30 x 0.6219 + 0.50 x 0.8393 + 0.20 x 0.9782 = 0.8019.
probability_weighted.band_note: House/street band collapses -- no SBC exists for a unit trust; band_position is null by convention for SBC-zero tickers.

sanity_check.description: P/E and EV/EBITDA trip tests are NOT APPLICABLE to this vehicle and were not computed: there is no EBITDA (no operations -- the Fund holds one financial asset), and accounting earnings are FVTPL revaluation noise (NI swung from -$1.688m to +$1.314m on marks alone), so any implied P/E would be meaningless. The valid analogue for a NAV vehicle is price-to-NAV, run below.
sanity_check.trip_conditions_checked: Trip if base-case IV implies P/NAV materially above ~1.05x, or base-case upside exceeds +100%. Neither fires: base IV implies 0.645x NAV and upside is NEGATIVE (-35.6%). The model is not manufacturing upside.
sanity_check.historical_pnav_context: PLP has traded at roughly parity to NAV since listing (price history effectively only from Dec-2023; NZX-listed since Sept-2019), and currently sits at a slight PREMIUM (1.00-1.01x). That parity is anomalous for a listed wrapper over unlisted assets and is best explained by the 95.5% captive related-party register and ~4.5% free float -- the market price is not an independent test of the manager's NAV. The base IV of 0.645x NAV diverges from that trading history not because the model expects the quoted price to fall to 0.645x, but because the price of a fair 14% expected return on this fund's realistic distribution-plus-growth stream is far below its NAV: the assets are priced (by the manager) to yield well under any defensible required return for their risk. Equivalently, buying at $1.304 locks in roughly a 4-5% expected total return -- the fund's own realised 5-year experience -- with mid-teens-risk exposure.
sanity_check.note: passed: true means the mechanical trip conditions (excess upside / excess implied P/NAV) did not fire and the negative verdict is internally consistent. It does not mean the price is safe: the check's central observation is that the usual listed-fund margin of safety (a discount to NAV) is entirely absent here.

verdict: At NZ$1.304 the units trade at a slight premium to the June-2026 NAV of $1.3010 -- pricing set by a ~4.5% free float, with no discount-to-NAV margin of safety to capture. The underlying stream a buyer actually receives -- a ~2.5% distribution yield plus NAV growth that has been NEGATIVE for three straight years against a 6.5% target -- is worth roughly $0.84 in the base case (-36%) and $0.80 probability-weighted (-38%) at a 14% cost of equity built for illiquid, manager-marked, Rolleston-concentrated rural property. The conclusion survives the discount rate: even at a bare 9% the base stream is worth ~$1.04, ~20% below the price. With rising look-through gearing (PLPP borrowings up ~4x to $13.75m in FY2026), distributions exceeding accounting earnings, and the manager facing an FMA trial in February 2027, the current price is not attractive on this analysis; the entry price for a 15% hurdle is ~$0.81.
